items.q: What is the cheapest alternative to HubSpot?
items.a: It depends on which piece of HubSpot's Marketing Hub you actually pay for, since HubSpot itself starts at $20 a seat a month on Starter. A team that only needs a sales pipeline, not a shared marketing record, pays a bit more on Pipedrive, which starts at $24 a month per seat with a 14-day trial and no onboarding fee. A team whose real need is marketing automation without full CRM breadth actually pays less with ActiveCampaign, whose cheapest plan bundles automation and a light CRM for about $15 a month billed annually at 1,000 contacts. Zoho CRM matches Starter's $20 a seat a month for a straight CRM swap, with no contact-count tier to grow into. None of the three replicate HubSpot's shared record across marketing, sales, service and content hubs; each replaces only the one job a specific business actually uses HubSpot for.

items.q: Is there a free alternative to HubSpot's CRM?
items.a: Yes, several tools in HubSpot's category have a genuine no-cost tier, though each covers only part of what HubSpot's own free tools do. Zoho CRM's Free edition covers up to 3 users with workflow automation and no credit card required, one more user than HubSpot's free cap of 2, though it has no mass email feature at all. Systeme.io's Free plan covers 2,000 contacts, sales funnels and one course at no cost, twice HubSpot's free 1,000 contacts, though free accounts stop taking new payments once lifetime sales pass USD 10,000 and a short grace window ends. Klaviyo's Free plan covers up to 250 active profiles with email and a small monthly allowance of SMS usage included, which HubSpot's free tools don't offer at any size. Match the free plan to the one feature that matters most, since none of these three copies HubSpot's specific combination of a free shared CRM plus free marketing tools.

items.q: What happens to your data if you cancel HubSpot?
items.a: HubSpot's customer agreement doesn't let you cancel or drop to a cheaper tier in the middle of your current term, and it won't refund fees already paid for months you don't use. To stop a plan from renewing at all, you turn off auto-renewal in the Account & Billing section of your account before the term ends; miss that window and the agreement renews you for another term of the same length, up to a year. What the terms do say plainly is that, short of a for-cause termination, your account keeps running on the Free Services once a paid subscription ends rather than being deleted outright. What isn't spelled out publicly is what happens to seats, workflows or contacts sitting above the free tier's caps of 2 users and 1,000 contacts once that switch happens, so ask HubSpot directly and treat anything above those numbers as something to record or export before your term lapses, not after.

items.q: Which HubSpot alternative is best for a team that only needs a sales pipeline, not a marketing hub?
items.a: Pipedrive is the more direct swap, since it's built as a sales-pipeline CRM rather than a set of marketing, service and content hubs bundled together. It bills strictly per seat across four plans, starting at $24 a month on Lite, with a 14-day trial that needs no card and no onboarding fee at any tier. Zoho CRM is the other real option: its Standard edition runs $20 a seat a month with workflow automation included and no contact-count tier to budget around, though its mass email sending is capped per organization per day rather than scaled to team size. Neither replicates HubSpot's shared record across marketing and sales, so a team that later wants campaigns and forms feeding the same pipeline will eventually need a separate email tool alongside either one. For a pipeline-only need today, that trade is usually worth the lower bill.

items.q: Do any HubSpot alternatives include marketing SMS without forcing an expensive upgrade?
items.a: Two do, and they price it differently than HubSpot does. Klaviyo sells SMS on every plan, including its free one, which comes with a small monthly allowance of mobile-messaging usage built in at no extra cost; paid usage bills per segment with carrier fees already included in the rate. GoHighLevel includes texting as metered usage on every plan too, starting with the $97-a-month Starter plan, once a one-time A2P 10DLC registration is done for U.S. numbers. HubSpot, by contrast, sells marketing SMS only as a $75-a-month add-on, and only with Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise, plans that start at $890 a month before the SMS add-on is even added. If native texting matters more than any other single feature, Klaviyo or GoHighLevel get you there without buying a much larger CRM tier first to unlock it.

items.q: Which HubSpot alternative doesn't require a 12-month contract?
items.a: Most of the field, actually. Zoho CRM is pay-as-you-go on every edition, monthly or yearly, and its own pricing FAQ says you can switch plans at any time with nothing to sign for a fixed term. GoHighLevel is month to month on every plan too, including the ones with its deepest automation, and you upgrade or cancel from the dashboard rather than a new contract. Pipedrive's plans come with a 14-day free trial and monthly billing that cancels at your next billing date; only its annual option is prepaid for the full year. Systeme.io's paid plans can be billed monthly as well, though downgrading isn't self-serve and goes through support instead. ActiveCampaign is the exception worth knowing about: its public pricing page shows only annual-billing rates, and while its help center confirms a monthly option exists in-account, that rate is never published anywhere public.

items.q: Which HubSpot alternative fits a freelancer or solo consultant best?
items.a: It depends on whether you need a full sales CRM or just a lighter one. Zoho CRM's Free edition covers up to 3 users, more than enough for a solo consultant, with workflow automation and no credit card required, though it caps storage at 5,000 records and can't send mass email at all. Pipedrive's Lite plan is built for exactly this size of user, at $24 a month for one seat, with a pipeline built around tracking deals rather than a marketing hub you'd rarely use fully. A freelancer selling anything productized, coaching, courses or a handful of digital products, fits Systeme.io better than either: its Free plan covers 2,000 contacts, sales funnels and one course at no cost, with a 0% transaction fee on every plan above it too. Pick based on whether you're managing a pipeline or selling directly to a list, since that's the real fork for a solo business, not price.
